subject.title: Feature: per-boot server-enforced internal capabilities for embedded cron and subagent completion

question: Should OpenClaw add a new per-boot internal-capability protocol for embedded cron and subagent completion, and which cross-process bootstrap boundary is acceptable?
rationale: The request creates a new authentication and authorization boundary that affects credential exposure, device pairing, cron authority, and session-finalization integrity; that permanent contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a capability design
options.body: Define the audiences, bootstrap transport, claims, replay semantics, and upgrade constraints before accepting a focused implementation.

options.title: Keep existing runtime identity only
options.body: Do not add cross-process capability delivery until a narrower supported embedded-runtime use case is agreed.

options.title: Design a generic prerequisite
options.body: First establish a reusable internal-principal Gateway API, then evaluate cron and completion as separate consumers.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a capability design
recommendation.body: Define the audiences, bootstrap transport, claims, replay semantics, and upgrade constraints before accepting a focused implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied evidence identifies only the report author; source history was unavailable for stronger routing.
